brief: Thomas the apostle is mentioned only in the lists of apostles in the first three Gospels, but features more significantly at three points in the Fourth Gospel. He urges the disciples to go with Jesus to Judaea, “that we may die with him”. In Jerusalem he does not know Jesus’ way, and so provides the cue for the announcement that Jesus is the way, the truth and the life. After doubting the resurrection, Thomas is convinced by seeing Jesus alive, and says, “My Lord and my God!” But the truly blessed are those who believe without seeing.
